objectives.title: Mad Hatter
objectives.prompt: "Why is a raven like a writing desk?" Wonderland runs CI on Jenkins, building the Wonderland/mad-hatter application repository (hosted on Gitea) on every branch and pull request. You have write access to that application repo — but the pipeline's Jenkinsfile is not in it. It lives in a separate, protected repository (Wonderland/mad-hatter-pipeline) that you can read but not modify, so you cannot poison the pipeline directly. The pipeline runs `make` inside the application checkout with Wonderland's release token, flag3, bound into the build environment. Edit the application's Makefile so that `make` prints flag3 in a form the console will not mask, push the branch and open a pull request. When the pipeline runs, read the build's console output, recover the value, and submit the flag.
hints: You cannot edit the Jenkinsfile — it is in Wonderland/mad-hatter-pipeline, which you can only read. But read it: it runs `make` inside the mad-hatter application checkout with flag3 bound as the FLAG environment variable. You CAN edit the application's Makefile.

Change the Makefile's default target so `make` exfiltrates the token, e.g. `echo "$FLAG" | rev | base64`. Jenkins masks a bound credential's value in the console — and, on modern versions, its plain base64 too; reversing before base64 evades the masker, and you undo it to recover the flag.

The multibranch pipeline builds every branch of the application repo and rescans about once a minute. Push your branch (and open a pull request); the build starts on its own. Read it under the wonderland-mad-hatter job, then `base64 -d <blob> | rev`.
